about: B1 (A6): under M89 every positioning block runs the defined cycle, and a polar move is one. LP, CP and CTP (pole: use) write their end point around the pole in PR and PA, not in axis words, so a block such as LP PA+60 moves the tool although it holds no X, Y or Z. The pole itself (CC, pole: set) still moves nothing.

states.about: The pole before the modal call: no move, no cycle.
Rule 4: M89 runs the cycle in its own block and starts the modal call.
A polar straight line with only an angle is a positioning block.
The same with an incremental angle.
A polar arc ends at a position as well.
So does a tangential polar arc.
A new pole moves nothing, so the cycle does not run, and the modal call stays.
M99 on a polar move runs the cycle once and ends the modal call.
After M99 a polar move runs nothing.
